title: Vodafone 借助 Data Engineering Agent 将数据管道成本降低 30%
author: Helena Guerra, Pedro Esteves
content:
For large organizations, building and maintaining data pipelines is one of the most complex tasks that data engineering teams are tasked with. In BigQuery environments, the Data Engineering Agent can help, leveraging Gemini to to automate these workflows.

In this blog post, Vodafone Czech Republic describes how it has used the Data Engineering Agent to modernize and optimize BigQuery stored procedures, transforming them into modern data pipelines and reducing pipeline execution times by half. - Pedro Esteves, Google Cloud

The Data Engineering Agent makes it easy to build and maintain modern data pipelines. The agent is available in BigQuery pipelines and Dataform. At Vodafone, we used the agent directly in Dataform to build Dataform pipelines. As shown in the example below, the Data Engineering Agent takes natural language instructions together with any code provided in the instruction file to build the Dataform pipeline.

How Vodafone currently executes its pipelines

Vodafone Czech Republic uses many BigQuery stored procedures to transform data for business purposes. These stored procedures are a legacy of a previous on-premises data warehouse migration to BigQuery. Many of them contain 2,000 or 3,000 lines of code and run sequentially.

Compared to a modular Dataform approach created by the Data Engineering Agent, there are several known disadvantages of maintaining legacy, multi-thousand-line stored procedures, as described in the table below.

Feature

Legacy stored procedures (Monolith)

Modular approach (Dataform)

Code structure

Single file, 1000s of lines, complex logic mixed.

Small, modular .sqlx files 

Logic reuse

Copy/Paste code blocks (prone to drift).

functions and ref() for strict logic reuse

Testing

Manual, ad-hoc, rarely done

Automated testing (Unique, Not Null, Referential Integrity) built-in

Documentation

Comments in code (usually outdated)

Auto-generated documentation with lineage graph

Execution

Manual scheduling; hard-coded dependency management

Automatic execution based on lineage (DAG)

How the Data Engineering Agent improved our data pipelines

To solve the problems of running and maintaining legacy stored procedures, we used the Data Engineering Agent to migrate some of the stored procedures into Dataform pipelines.

Parallelization of code

The Data Engineering Agent was able to parallelize the code into independent steps which are then run in parallel to improve readability and performance. See the example below:

Caching intermediate results

The Data Engineering Agent can understand dependencies between the tables and cache certain intermediate tables using BigQuery materialized views. This means that tables that are used in downstream processes can be cached, speeding up code execution and reducing cost.

Facilitating orchestration of the pipeline

Having a modular pipeline allows us to facilitate end-to-end orchestration and pipeline dependencies to meet our SLAs. Before using Dataform, we had to manually control pipeline execution by creating metadata tables with several checkpoints and logs. Dependencies between stored procedures jobs were also maintained manually in a spreadsheet. By executing the pipeline in Dataform, all the dependencies and execution logs are handled by Dataform. 

Ability to run sections of the pipeline

Because the code is now split into several steps, it’s possible to execute only a subset of the actions in Dataform rather than running the entire stored procedure. This can help with debugging and gives us the flexibility to only run the relevant sections of the code.

Lessons learned

  1. There’s a trade-off between parallelization and caching. When we prompted the Data Engineering Agent to parallelize our procedures, we noticed an increase in cost.

  2. When running a standard sequential stored procedure, BigQuery caches the base table for the first thread. However, splitting this logic into parallel streams can inadvertently negate those caching benefits, causing full table scans for each thread. 

  3. To solve this, we asked the Data Engineering Agent to create materialized views for intermediate tables. These views effectively pre-cache the data, ensuring that your parallelized queries remain performant and cost-efficient.

  4. To make the agent parallelize the code more efficiently we gave it specific instructions on which areas (staging tables) we were interested in parallelizing. 

Results: Accelerated migration and performance

Deploying Data Engineering Agent delivered immediate and measurable impact, specifically in addressing the toil associated with legacy migrations. The agent successfully achieved high-fidelity replication of all stored procedures, ensuring 1:1 logic parity with minimal human intervention.

By automating the conversion of complex ETL pipelines, the agent achieved a 90% reduction in migration time compared with traditional manual approaches. What would have typically required weeks of engineering effort was completed in a fraction of the time, freeing engineers to focus on other key tasks.

Furthermore, the modernization of the underlying infrastructure resulted in substantial performance gains. Post-migration benchmarks indicate that the new data pipelines run twice as fast, significantly reducing query latency and increasing overall data throughput.

And as we previously discussed, instructing the agent to cache intermediate tables led to a 30% reduction in costs.

Beyond accelerating development and reducing costs, these agentic tools are also changing the way data engineers approach their work. Rather than spending significant time on repetitive migration and optimization tasks, engineers can collaborate with agents to explore different implementation options, validate design decisions, and accelerate delivery. This shift is encouraging teams to adopt new ways of working, where agentic capabilities become an integral part of the development process and help shape how data solutions are designed, delivered, and maintained.

Industrializing the Data Engineering Agent at Vodafone

At Vodafone, we’re planning to scale the use of the Data Engineering Agent across the company in the following key areas:

  • Standardized Dataform template repository: Establishing a central repository for Dataform templates allows for consistent architecture and design patterns across different projects and teams, helping ensure quality and alignment with global standards.

  • Global market onboarding: We will expand the Data Engineering Agent deployment across key Vodafone markets including the Czech Republic (CZ), Romania (RO), Ireland (IE), Germany (DE), and the United Kingdom (UK), to drive widespread adoption and modernization.

  • Integration with developer environments (IDEs): Deepening the integration of agentic capabilities directly into developer workflows (such as VS Code, and and Antigravity) will enable engineers to leverage Data Engineering Agent features within their existing tools and IDEs.

  • Federated CI/CD governance: Implementing a centralized yet flexible governance framework for Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) will allow individual markets to maintain autonomy while adhering to corporate quality and security policies.

  • Modernization of legacy stored procedures at scale: By systematically migrating complex, legacy workloads — specifically SAS code, BTEQ scripts, and MicroStrategy — into modern Dataform pipelines will allow us to reduce technical debt and accelerate transformation across the enterprise.

To learn more about transforming your enterprise data architecture for the agentic era, download our complete Data Agents Guidebook or explore Google Cloud’s Rapid Migration and Modernization Program (RaMP). To get started building and optimizing your own data pipelines with the agent today, visit the Data Engineering Agent pipelines documentation.

oneSentenceSummary: Vodafone Czech Republic 使用 Data Engineering Agent 将旧版 BigQuery 存储过程现代化为模块化 Dataform 管道，实现迁移速度提升 90%、执行时间缩短 50%，并通过并行化和物化视图节省 30% 的成本。
summary: Vodafone Czech Republic 借助 Gemini 驱动的 Data Engineering Agent，将旧版 BigQuery 存储过程（每个包含 2，000-3，000 行代码）迁移为模块化 Dataform 管道。该智能体自动完成转换流程，与手动方式相比，迁移时间减少 90%。现代化后的管道运行速度提升一倍，并通过并行化以及为中间结果创建物化视图，将成本降低 30%。主要改进包括模块化代码结构、自动化测试、自动生成的文档和数据血缘图，以及基于 DAG 的执行方式。团队发现，并行化可能会因抵消缓存带来的收益而增加成本，随后通过创建物化视图解决了这一问题。未来计划包括在 Vodafone 各市场推广、统一 Dataform 模板、集成 IDE，以及建立联邦式 CI/CD 治理机制。

mainPoints.point: 自动将旧版存储过程迁移至现代化 Dataform 管道
mainPoints.explanation: Data Engineering Agent 将包含 2，000-3，000 行代码的单体存储过程转换为模块化的 .sqlx 文件，并自动完成测试和文档生成，采用基于 DAG 的执行方式，使迁移时间减少 90%。

mainPoints.point: 并行化与物化视图使成本降低 30%、执行速度提升 50%
mainPoints.explanation: 通过将代码拆分为并行步骤，并借助 BigQuery 物化视图缓存中间结果，Vodafone 将管道成本降低 30%，执行时间缩短一半。不过，并行化需要谨慎处理，以免抵消 BigQuery 原生缓存的收益。

mainPoints.point: 智能体工具推动协作式数据工程工作流
mainPoints.explanation: 工程师如今可以与智能体协作，探索不同的实现方案并验证设计决策，从重复性的迁移工作转向更具战略性的开发任务；智能体则会自动处理 90% 的转换逻辑。

mainPoints.point: 将智能体能力推广至 Vodafone 全球业务
mainPoints.explanation: Vodafone 计划在 CZ、RO、IE、DE 和 UK 市场扩大 Data Engineering Agent 的部署范围，建立标准化的 Dataform 模板，集成 IDE，并实施联邦式 CI/CD 治理，推动企业级现代化。
